hypothesis: A more responsive chronological Elo strength representation can improve the current 13-feature logistic T20 models. K is selected only on validation log loss from a predeclared grid; all other features, estimator, population and chronological split rules remain unchanged.

reference_policy.female: raw logistic W0; calibrator not promoted

male.reason: The K=80 challenger improves every primary metric on the frozen 513-match test and wins accuracy, log loss, Brier and AUC in all five rolling-origin windows plus the 171-match future holdout. ECE improves on the main test and 3/5 rolling windows, but worsens on the future holdout. The strength improvement is therefore robust, but probability calibration should be resolved before replacing the production reference.

female.reason: The K=160 challenger improves accuracy, log loss, Brier and AUC on the frozen 310-match test and in all five rolling-origin windows. Main-test ECE is worse, but the 171-match future holdout reverses that and improves ECE as well. Because W0 production explicitly uses raw probabilities, the calibrated challenger is diagnostic only; a production replacement should first establish whether the improved strength representation retains calibration under the final production protocol.

implementation_note: The initial Challenger B runner used percentage-derived boundaries that would produce 2387/512/512 for men rather than the frozen 2387/511/513 contract. That implementation was corrected before these results were accepted. The final runner asserts the exact frozen split counts.
